judgements.reason: PDE still needs trace and extension operators on Lipschitz domains, Riesz-Thorin and Calderon-Zygmund theory, Schauder and De Giorgi-Nash-Moser regularity, and Galerkin/heat-semigroup parabolic theory, each a deep analytic layer. GNF's remaining power-saving ray-class count, idelic compactness and ray-class dictionary, adelic base change, Hecke characters and Picard groups of orders are classical number theory built directly on Mathlib's adeles, and its ray class groups already exist.

CHF must still prove grid invariance, build the bigraded F[U] structure theory and tau with the Milnor-conjecture and slice-genus bounds, and construct stable HF-hat from scratch. It also takes smooth knot theory (Reidemeister moves, Cromwell adequacy) and cobordism normal forms from the unbuilt GeometricTopology layer. PDE's missing trace, Calderon-Zygmund, Schauder, De Giorgi-Nash-Moser and parabolic lanes are heavy but self-contained real analysis, and its Dirichlet problem and spectrum are already built.

AC needs Szemeredi's theorem, Gowers norms with nilmanifold equidistribution and the Green-Tao-Ziegler inverse theorem, transference, and linear equations in primes, on top of prime-number-theorem and sieve inputs from AnalyticNumberTheory and SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns. CHF's missing grid invariance, tau, lattice homology and stable HF-hat are finite combinatorics and homological algebra over F2[U], even counting its knot-theory reconciliation.

AF must build adelic reductive groups with reduction theory and the representation theory of both real groups ((g,K)-modules, Casselman-Wallach globalization, van Est) and p-adic groups (Jacquet functors, second adjointness) before automorphic forms, cusp forms and the finiteness theorems. AC's Green-Tao-Ziegler inverse theorem, nilsequence equidistribution and linear equations in primes form one very deep tower, but it rests on finite Fourier analysis, graph regularity and Roth's theorem, which Mathlib already has.

FF needs p-divisible groups, Dieudonne and crystalline theory, and the Kisin and Fontaine-Laffaille classifications. These sit on imported period rings and crystalline representations (with perfectoid tilting), algebraic spaces, abelian-scheme duality and cotangent complexes. AF's essential imports are adelic groups and smooth representations; its algebraic-moduli and GAGA closure enters only through AF.5's normalisation edge, and it starts from Tau Ceti's reductive groups and Peter-Weyl theorem and Mathlib's adeles.

FF's Breuil-Kisin and Fontaine-Laffaille classifications need period rings, crystalline representations, crystals and Dieudonne theory stacked beneath them. TB's Berkovich spaces, metric-graph Riemann-Roch, tropicalization and Chambert-Loir measures need only formal and adic generic fibres, semistable reduction and intersection numbers on models, from SchemeAndStackFoundations and AdicSpacesPartII.

Before cotangent complexes, derived completion and derived de Rham can exist, DDR needs the whole infinity-categorical enhancement (a quasicategory model, presentability and the adjoint functor theorem, symmetric monoidal structure, animated rings) as well as PD envelopes, crystalline sites and the PD Poincare lemma. TB's Berkovich analytic spaces, skeletons, tropicalization and model measures are substantial, but they rest on semistable reduction, formal generic fibres and Tau Ceti's Huber/Spa foundations.

Before the main conjecture, ESC needs global class field theory, Poitou-Tate duality, Iwasawa algebras, Coleman power series, Kubota-Leopoldt, Baker-Brumer and Ferrero-Washington, plus the full Euler/Kolyvagin-system machinery. Even without its inessential Bloch-Kato import, which would add DD.1 and the infinity-categorical stages, this is broader than DDR's single deep tower of infinity-categorical enhancement, crystalline cohomology and derived de Rham.

SKO sits on a tower the library lacks entirely: classifying spaces, Quillen's theorems, the plus construction and spectra, and the Q- and S-construction machines with localization and nonconnective K-theory. Only then come Thomason-Trobaugh localization, Gersten, Adams operations and GRR for schemes. ESC's class field theory, Poitou-Tate, Iwasawa, Coleman, Kubota-Leopoldt and Euler-system layers are as broad, but less deeply stacked and closer to Tau Ceti's profinite cohomology.

KTFLF's closure contains all of SKO and its K-theory stack. On top of that it needs the norm-residue theorem, the motivic spectral sequence and etale K-theory (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.1-M.7), THH/TC trace methods, de Rham-Witt complexes, and Hesselholt-Madsen's local computations.

Kato needs Galois representations of modular forms through ell-adic etale cohomology with weights, p-adic comparison theorems via A_inf and perfectoid geometry, (phi,Gamma)-modules and Perrin-Riou's logarithm, overconvergent modular symbols, and the full Euler-system, main-conjecture and class-field-theory machinery (426 upstream stages). KTFLF's K-theory stack, norm-residue theorem, motivic spectral sequence and THH/TC computations are enormous but form a much smaller closure (114 stages).

Kato's imports span ell-adic cohomology with Deligne's weights, p-adic comparison through perfectoid and A_inf geometry, (phi,Gamma)-modules, modular symbols, and all the Euler-system and Iwasawa machinery (426 upstream stages). MET's own norm-residue proof, higher Chow groups, motivic spectral sequence and regulators, on an imported K-theory stack and Borel's theorem (144 stages), add up to less, and Kato uses MET's etale Chern classes only on K_2 symbols.

Hecke needs essentially all of Fargues-Scholze below Chapter IX, plus classical ell-adic cohomology with weights (208 upstream stages). That means perfectoid spaces, diamonds and v-stacks with their etale six operations, condensed/solid and lisse sheaves, the relative Fargues-Fontaine curve, Bun_G and geometric Satake. MET's norm-residue theorem, motivic spectral sequence and Borel/p-adic regulators on the K-theory stack (144 stages) are comparably deep but somewhat less in total.

FF needs p-divisible groups and Dieudonne, Fontaine-Laffaille and Breuil-Kisin theory, built on imported period rings, crystalline cohomology, algebraic spaces and abelian schemes. GNF's remaining ray-class counting, idelic compactness, Hecke characters and Picard groups of orders are classical number theory on Mathlib's adeles, and its ray class groups and weak approximation already exist.

Hecke's closure already contains DD.0-DD.2, DD.5, the infinity-categorical enhancement and crystalline theory. On top of those it needs all of Fargues-Scholze (diamonds, etale six operations, the Fargues-Fontaine curve, Bun_G, geometric Satake) and ell-adic weights. DDR needs only its infinity-categorical base and crystalline cohomology beneath derived de Rham.

SKO must build higher algebraic K-theory from spaces and spectra up (plus construction, Q- and S-constructions, localization and nonconnective theorems) before Thomason-Trobaugh localization, Gersten, Adams operations and GRR. TB's Berkovich spaces, skeletons, metric-graph divisors and tropicalization need only semistable reduction, intersection numbers on models and formal generic fibres.

KTFLF contains SKO's whole K-theory tower and adds the norm-residue theorem, the motivic spectral sequence, etale K-theory and THH/TC trace methods (114 upstream stages). ESC's class field theory, Poitou-Tate, Iwasawa, Coleman, Kubota-Leopoldt and Euler-system layers amount to less, and much of its 77-stage closure comes from an inessential Bloch-Kato import.

AF must build adelic reductive groups with reduction theory, then real and p-adic representation theory (Casselman-Wallach, van Est, Jacquet functors, second adjointness), and only then automorphic forms, cusp forms and rationality. PDE's missing trace, Calderon-Zygmund, Schauder, De Giorgi-Nash-Moser and parabolic theory is self-contained analysis, and the library already has its Sobolev spaces, Dirichlet problem and Hille-Yosida theorem.

Hecke needs the whole Fargues-Scholze apparatus (perfectoid spaces, diamonds, etale six operations, the Fargues-Fontaine curve, Bun_G, geometric Satake) and classical ell-adic weights. AC's tower of Szemeredi, Green-Tao-Ziegler and linear equations in primes, with its sieve and prime-number-theorem inputs, is deep but far smaller, and it rests on Mathlib's finite Fourier analysis and Roth's theorem.

CHF must still prove grid invariance, develop the bigraded F[U] structure theory, tau and its unknotting and slice-genus bounds, build stable HF-hat from scratch, and reconcile with smooth knots from the unbuilt GeometricTopology layer. GNF's remaining ray-class counting, idelic compactness and ray-class dictionary, adelic base change, Hecke characters and orders sit directly on Mathlib's number-field and adele library, and its Layers 0-2 are built.

Both need the K-theory stack, SchemeKTheoryOperations, and MET's M.1-M.7 with the norm-residue theorem. MET adds the M.8 regulators with Borel's theorem, p-adic Hodge regulators, Bloch groups and Quillen's finite generation (144 upstream stages). KTFLF instead adds THH/TC trace methods, de Rham-Witt and the Hesselholt-Madsen computations (114).

Kato needs Galois representations of modular forms with ell-adic weights, p-adic comparison through perfectoid and A_inf geometry, (phi,Gamma)-modules, and the Euler-system and main-conjecture machinery (426 upstream stages). TB's Berkovich, skeleton and tropical theory needs only semistable reduction, intersection numbers on models and formal generic fibres (11 stages).

DDR must first build an infinity-categorical enhancement (quasicategories, presentability, the adjoint functor theorem, symmetric monoidal structure, animated rings) and crystalline cohomology, and only then cotangent complexes, derived completion and filtered derived de Rham. That is a taller stack with little library support. AC's Szemeredi, Green-Tao-Ziegler, transference and linear-equations-in-primes proofs are very long, but they rest on Mathlib's finite Fourier analysis, regularity lemma and Roth's theorem plus sieve and prime-number-theorem inputs.

ESC needs class field theory, Poitou-Tate duality, Iwasawa algebras, Coleman power series, Kubota-Leopoldt, Baker-Brumer and Ferrero-Washington, and the Euler/Kolyvagin-system machinery. CHF's remaining grid invariance, tau bounds, lattice homology and stable HF-hat are finite combinatorics and homological algebra, plus a knot-theory reconciliation.
